sentences.text:
The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 Criminal Petition No.5868 of 2020
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.109 of 2019 on the file of the Court of the learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur, wherein the petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 were alleged to have committed the offences punishable under Sections 353, 188, 272 and 273 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'I.P.C.') and Sections 26 and 59(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case of the prosecution is that petitioner No.1 was allegedly selling the prohibited tobacco products at higher prices and he confessed the same in the presence of the mediators, by stating that petitioner No.2 sold the said products to him.

Therefore, the petitioners were arrested, the tobacco products were seized and crime No.14 of 2018 was registered for the aforementioned offences,
which resulted in filing of the above C.C.

3. Heard Sri Raja Reddy Koneti, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that Sections 328, 272 and 273 I.P.C. and 59(i) of FSS Act relate to food safety standards.
Section 328 I.P.C. speaks about causing hurt by means of poison with an intention to commit an offence.
Section 272 I.P.C. speaks about adulteration of food or drink intended for sale and Section 273 of I.P.C. speaks about sale of Noxious Food or Drink.

He further submits that possession, sale, purchase and transport of banned tobacco products will not attract the offences as alleged and the Police have no power to register the offences under above Sections except the designated officers like Food Safety Officer.
LK,J 5.

Learned Counsel for the petitioners has placed reliance on the common order, dated 18.12.2019,
passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch,
wherein it was held that tobacco does not fall within the definition of "food" as specified under Section 3(i)(j) of the FSS Act.
Therefore, registration of FIR is not permissible.
He further submits that in terms of the said order passed in Criminal Petition Nos.5421 of 2019 and batch, this Court has allowed several criminal petitions by quashing respective F.I.Rs.
Hence, he submits that in terms of the aforesaid orders, this Criminal Petition may be allowed.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor has not disputed the fact that in similar circumstances several F.I.Rs. were quashed by this Court.
